# inventory-migrate.tsv — whitespace/tab separated; lines starting with # are ignored
# columns (ALL required):  old_node  old_ctid  new_ctid  new_node  storage
#   old_node : host/IP of the source node (ssh reachable from storage-node via key)
#   old_ctid : VMID on the old node (must be RUNNING to sync)
#   new_ctid : VMID to create on the target node (must be free)
#   new_node : host/IP of the target node for THIS CT (REQUIRED — no default;
#              a row without new_node is skipped with an ERROR in the log)
#   storage  : PVE storage id for THIS CT (REQUIRED — no default). It must exist
#              on BOTH sides with the SAME id and DIFFERENT types:
#                this node : dir  -> pvesm add dir tank-hdd-nas \
#                                      --path /tank/hosting --is_mountpoint yes
#                new_node  : nfs  -> same dataset over NFS, same id, so the
#                                    volume id in the CT config resolves there
#              The engine derives the pool path from PVE itself (pvesm path),
#              so there is nothing else to keep in sync by hand.
#   rootfs size is derived from the old CT automatically (no size column)
#   network is NOT written into the new config; add net0 by hand at go-live
# run one cron schedule per storage:
#   ct-migrate.sh --storage tank-hdd-nas
#   ct-migrate.sh --storage tank-ssd-nas
# and set LANES in ctmig.conf to how many of those can overlap, so the
# tool-wide bandwidth ceiling still holds.
# example — CTs split across two target nodes and two storages:
# old_node    old_ctid  new_ctid  new_node      storage
